title: Ask first
caption: The questions you ask before a treatment matter more than most people realise. Not because clinics are hiding things, but because the right questions shift you from passenger to participant. Who is trained to do this, what happens if the result isn't what you expected, and how many sessions does 'a course' actually mean — these aren't awkward to ask, they're basic. Knowing what to ask before you book is how you stay in control of the outcome. Not medical advice, just the honest basics. Learn more at cliniclick.ae

slides.headline: Who is doing this procedure?
slides.sub: Qualification and training level vary — it's worth asking directly.

slides.headline: What if I don't like the result?
slides.sub: Some treatments are reversible, some aren't — know which applies here.

slides.headline: How many sessions until I see anything?
slides.sub: 'A course of treatment' can mean two sessions or twelve.

slides.headline: What's the downtime, really?
slides.sub: Marketing language and actual recovery time are often very different numbers.

slides.sub: The honest basics on every treatment, in one place.
